learning_outcomes.text: Knows the principles of production and manufacturing systems. Applies environmental technologies and values sustainability.
Values the environmental and ergonomic implications of production processes.
Applies quality criteria in material reception and manufacturing process control.
Applies knowledge of mechanical technology to the design of manufacturing systems.
Knows the treatments a material can undergo to modify its behavior. Selects the most suitable materials for each application and the state in which they should be used.
Knows the principles of manufacturing metallic elements, casting, machining, and plastic deformation. Defines the selection processes and parameters for the elaboration of plastic elements.
Evaluates the environmental and sustainability consequences of different production processes.
Programs numerical control systems. Plans and tests different metal welding systems. Plans and executes metrology operations.

syllabus_topics: Forming processes (Forging, Rolling, Extrusion, Drawing, Upsetting)
Sheet metal forming (Stamping, Deep drawing, Bending, Cutting)
Procedures: Soft soldering, Brazing, Oxy-gas welding, Electric arc welding, Resistance welding and other procedures
teaching_methods: Introductory activities: Introduction to the subject and explanation of regulations.
Lecture session: Contents will be explained in these sessions.
Problem/exercise solving: These sessions will be dedicated to applying the contents of the lecture sessions.
Presentations/expositions: The manufacturing project will be presented.
Personalized attention: Personalized attention will be provided to students who request it.
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, the minimum grade for the weighted average of the exams and the manufacturing project must be higher than 4 points. The second sitting will consist of an exam covering 100% of the course content. Fraudulent use of AI or any other means in assessment activities will result in a failing grade for that activity.
